subject: Plotting coefficients in mixedmirt, and unipolar item response models

messages.author: 587d84954f4c4064
messages.subject: Plotting coefficients in mixedmirt, and unipolar item response models
parts:
Hello, all,

Please be gentle to me as I mainly use Stata, and I'm starting to convert to R. I'll be using the mirt package for my dissertation.

In much of my work, I've found it very useful to use dot and whisker plots of regression coefficients, as the the R package dotwhisker does. I intend to used mixedmirt to fit a regression to an IRT-estimated latent trait, and I don't see any functionality native to mixedmirt that would enable me to plot the regression coefficients (as opposed to the item characteristic curves and such). I also know that dotwhisker won't accept objects of the classes produced by mixedmirt. Does anyone have suggestions how to plot regression coefficients from mixedmirt?

Also, the above-mentioned latent trait is depression. Unipolar IRT models like the log-logistic model have been proposed for unipolar traits like depression and other forms of psychopathology. In health services research, which is my field, I believe a lot of the traits we're interested in are better modeled by unipolar models, rather than bipolar models. If unipolar models aren't on Phil's radar already, I'd love to put them on, and ask if he'd consider implementing them in the future.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Plotting coefficients in mixedmirt, and unipolar item response models
parts:
These models could be fit in mirt using some of the customized input methods. Namely, the createItem() and createGroup() function to build these customized IRT probability models (the former), and specifying a log-normal prior density function for theta (the latter). You'd also need to provide a new Theta grid to integrate over since negative thetas in the quadrature grid would not be valid under these models. Estimation will be fairly slow given that numerical derivatives and such will be used (unless you provide the derivative functions yourself....in which case feel free to contact me since I'd be willing to add these models into the core package if the Hessian and gradient code were already written). Not sure about starting values for these models, but you may know more about what will be reasonable for  your datasets anyway. HTH.

Phil

messages.author: 587d84954f4c4064
messages.subject: Re: Plotting coefficients in mixedmirt, and unipolar item response models
parts:
Phil, thanks for the response!

For plotting the coefficients in mixedmirt(), the dotwhisker package I mentioned earlier can do this. I was merely unaware that I needed to extract the results using one of the mirt functions, assign them to a data frame, and do some editing. Some example code stemming from my work for the group's benefit:

library(dotwhisker)
phq9_reg <- mixedmirt(phq_9_vars,phq_9_data,1,
lr.fixed = ~1+dx_anxiety+dx_depression+dx_bipolar+dx_schizophrenia+dx_psychotic+dx_ptsd+age+adl_long,
itemtype ='graded')
plot <-data.frame(coef(phq9_reg))
#transpose the data frame; required for dwplot to recognize the data frame's format
plot <- t(plot)
#extract the fixed effects only; the first 39 rows are all the discrimination and difficulty parameters
plot <- plot[40:47,]
#dotwhisker needs a column called term that takes on the row names
#You can edit this column to contain your actual variable names
plot$term <- rownames(plot)
#need to assign some specific names to the columns for dotwhisker to recognize and plot
names(plot) <-c("estimate","conf.low","conf.high","term")
dwplot(plot)




I'll be renaming the variables on my own time, and probably add a line through theta = 0, but this seems to do nicely. However, if anyone has a more parsimonious way to do it, I'd love to hear it.
